question: What should be considered during the planning stage before implementation begins?

results.chunk_text:
## 2. Planning

Features begin as a written proposal describing the problem, the proposed
approach, and rough scope. Proposals for anything larger than a small
change are reviewed in a weekly planning meeting where the team decides
whether to proceed, and if so, roughly how it fits into the current
quarter's priorities.

A proposal should explain the problem being addressed rather than focusing
only on the requested implementation. Where possible, the proposal should
identify the expected users, business outcome, dependencies, and constraints.
This helps the team distinguish between a genuine product requirement and a
technical solution that may need further discussion.

Planning should also consider whether the proposed work affects existing
services, APIs, databases, integrations, security controls, or operational
procedures. A feature that appears small from a user perspective may still
have significant technical consequences if it changes a shared component.

Before implementation begins, the team should have enough information to
understand what success looks like. The level of detail required depends on
the size of the work. A small maintenance change may only require a concise
ticket, while a larger feature may require acceptance criteria, technical
investigation, estimates, and a design document.

Dependencies should be identified early. If another team, service, vendor,
or infrastructure component is required, the owner and expected timing
should be recorded. Teams should avoid beginning implementation when a
critical dependency is unresolved unless the dependency can be safely
mocked or isolated.
results.title: DOC-016_software_development_lifecycle

results.chunk_text:
## 3. Design

For non-trivial features, an engineer writes a short design document
covering the technical approach, key trade-offs, and any impact on other
teams' systems. Design documents are reviewed asynchronously by at least
one senior engineer before implementation begins.

The design should explain the major components involved and how information
moves between them. It should identify important interfaces, data
structures, external dependencies, and expected failure conditions. The
purpose is not to document every line of code but to make significant
technical decisions visible before implementation becomes expensive to
change.

When multiple approaches are possible, the design should explain why the
selected approach is preferred. Factors may include simplicity,
maintainability, performance, reliability, compatibility with existing
systems, and operational cost.

question: What is the recommended approach for handling errors in code?

results.chunk_text:
## Error Handling

Errors should be handled at the layer that has enough context to decide
what to do about them. Swallowing an error silently is discouraged;
at minimum, an error should be logged with enough context to diagnose the
issue later.
results.title: DOC-017_coding_standards

results.chunk_text:
## 5. Code Review

Every change requires at least one approval before merging. Reviewers are
expected to check for correctness, readability, and test coverage, and to
leave specific, actionable feedback rather than vague comments. Authors
should respond to every comment, even if only to explain why a suggestion
was not taken.

Reviewers should consider the behavior of the change rather than focusing
only on formatting. Important questions include whether the implementation
matches the intended requirement, whether errors are handled appropriately,
and whether the change introduces unexpected side effects.

Reviewers should also consider maintainability. Code that works correctly
but is unnecessarily difficult to understand can increase future
maintenance cost. Clear naming, reasonable function boundaries, and
consistent project conventions should be preferred.

services, additional review may be appropriate. The r
results.title: DOC-016_software_development_lifecycle

results.chunk_text:
## Error Responses

Error responses include a machine-readable error code, a human-readable
message, and, where relevant, the specific field that caused a validation
error. Error codes are documented and stable; the wording of the
human-readable message may change without being considered a breaking
change.
results.title: DOC-019_api_design_guidelines

question: What approval is required for purchase requests above five thousand dollars?

results.chunk_text:
## Approval Thresholds

Purchase requests up to five thousand dollars require manager approval.
Requests above five thousand dollars require both manager and department
head approval, and requests above twenty-five thousand dollars additionally
require finance team review before a purchase order is issued.
results.title: DOC-028_procurement_procedure

results.chunk_text:
## Purchase Requests

Purchases over five hundred dollars require a purchase request submitted
through the procurement portal, including the business justification and
the budget code the purchase will be charged against. Purchases under this
threshold can generally be made directly by the employee and expensed
through the standard expense process.
results.title: DOC-028_procurement_procedure

results.chunk_text:
# Software Installation Request Process

Employees who need software not available in the standard IT catalog can
submit a request through the IT ticketing system. Requests should include
the software name, business justification, and whether the tool will
handle any company or customer data.

Requests are reviewed within three business days. Tools that handle
sensitive data require an additional security review, which can take up to
two weeks depending on the vendor's responsiveness to security
questionnaires. Free trials of unapproved software should not be installed
without submitting a request first, even for evaluation purposes.

Once approved, IT installs the software remotely for managed devices or
provides installation instructions for cases where remote installation is
not possible. Approved software is added to the internal catalog so future
requests for the same tool by other employees can be fast-tracked.
results.title: DOC-009_software_installation_request_process

question: What mandatory training must new hires complete by the end of their first week?

results.chunk_text:
## Week One

The first day begins with a welcome session led by People Operations,
followed by a laptop setup session with IT. Managers are expected to
schedule a one-on-one within the first three days to review team goals and
introduce the new hire to immediate teammates. Mandatory training modules
(security awareness, code of conduct, and workplace safety) must be
completed by the end of week one.
results.title: DOC-001_employee_onboarding_guide

results.chunk_text:

This guide walks new hires through their first two weeks at NexaCore Solutions.
It covers account setup, required training, and who to contact for common
questions during the first month.

All employees are required to review and acknowledge this Code of Conduct
annually through the HR portal. New hires acknowledge it as part of the
onboarding process during their first week.

question: What steps does an on-call engineer take to declare an incident?

results.chunk_text:
## 3. Declaring an Incident

An on-call engineer declares an incident by posting in the incident channel
and creating an incident record, which assigns an incident commander
responsible for coordinating the response. Declaring early, even before the
full scope is known, is preferred over waiting for certainty.
results.title: DOC-024_incident_management_runbook

results.chunk_text:
## 2. Detecting an Incident

Most incidents are detected automatically through monitoring alerts, though
some are first reported by customers through support. Any employee who
notices unusual behavior, such as a service being unreachable, should
report it in the #ops-incidents channel even if they are unsure whether it
qualifies as an incident.
results.title: DOC-024_incident_management_runbook

results.chunk_text:
## 4. Roles During an Incident

- Incident commander: coordinates response, makes final decisions, manages communication
- Technical lead: directs the technical investigation and fix
- Communications lead: updates the status page and internal stakeholders

Not every incident requires all three roles; smaller incidents may be
handled by a single engineer acting in all capacities.
results.title: DOC-024_incident_management_runbook

question: How is customer feedback triaged after it is received?

results.chunk_text:
# Customer Feedback Handling

Customer feedback arrives through several channels: in-app feedback forms,
support tickets, sales conversations, and direct outreach from the product
team. All feedback is logged in the shared feedback tracker regardless of
source, so patterns can be identified across channels rather than staying
siloed within one team.
results.title: DOC-023_customer_feedback_handling

results.chunk_text:
## Triage

Product managers triage new feedback weekly, tagging it by product area
and rough theme. Feedback that reveals a bug rather than a feature request
is redirected to engineering through the normal bug reporting process
instead of being tracked as a feature request.
results.title: DOC-023_customer_feedback_handling

results.chunk_text:
## Closing the Loop

When feedback leads to a shipped feature, customers who originally
requested it are notified where practically possible, since this is one of
the strongest signals customers get that their input is taken seriously.
Feedback that will not be actioned is also closed out with a brief
explanation rather than left open indefinitely.
results.title: DOC-023_customer_feedback_handling

question: What is required before an employee can receive elevated access to production or financial systems?

results.chunk_text:
## Elevated Access

Elevated access, such as production system access or financial system
access, requires a documented business justification and is time-limited
where practical. Elevated access is reviewed every quarter, and access that
is no longer needed is removed rather than left in place by default.
results.title: DOC-014_access_control_policy

results.chunk_text:
# Access Control Policy

Access to NexaCore Solutions systems is granted based on role and business
need, following the principle of least privilege described in the
Information Security Policy. New access is requested through the access
request portal and requires approval from the employee's manager and the
relevant system owner.
results.title: DOC-014_access_control_policy

results.chunk_text:
## 7. Third-Party and Vendor Access

Vendors requiring access to company systems must sign a data processing
agreement before access is granted. Vendor access is reviewed alongside
employee access during the quarterly access review and is removed promptly
when a vendor engagement ends.
results.title: DOC-011_information_security_policy

results.title: DOC-015_security_awareness_training_guide

results.chunk_text:
## 3. Reporting an Incident

Any employee who suspects a security incident should report it immediately
to IT Security through the incident hotline or the #security-incident
channel, rather than attempting to resolve it themselves. Early reporting,
even of something that turns out to be a false alarm, is always preferred
over delayed reporting.
results.title: DOC-012_incident_response_procedure

results.chunk_text:
# Password and Authentication Guidelines

All NexaCore Solutions accounts require multi-factor authentication in
addition to a password. Passwords must be at least twelve characters and
should not reuse a password from a personal account or a previous company
password.

The company password manager is the recommended way to generate and store
credentials for internal tools. Passwords should never be written down on
paper, stored in an unencrypted document, or shared over chat or email,
even with a manager or IT support.

If an account is suspected of being compromised, employees should change
the password immediately and report the incident to IT Security through
the helpdesk, marking the ticket as urgent. IT Security may temporarily
lock an account while an investigation is in progress.

Authentication tokens for automated systems and integrations should be
rotated every ninety days and stored in the approved secrets management
tool rather than in code or configuration files.
results.title: DOC-007_password_and_authentication_guidelines

question: How far in advance should planned leave requests be submitted?

results.chunk_text:
# Leave and Time Off Policy

NexaCore Solutions provides employees with paid time off, sick leave, and
public holidays. Full-time employees accrue fifteen days of paid time off
per year during their first three years, increasing to twenty days after
three years of continuous employment.

Leave requests should be submitted through the internal HR portal at least
five business days in advance for planned absences. Sick leave does not
require advance notice, but employees should notify their manager as early
as reasonably possible on the day of absence.

Unused paid time off may be carried over up to a maximum of five days into
the following calendar year. Carried-over days must be used within the
first quarter or they are forfeited. Employees on approved parental leave
continue to accrue time off during the leave period in accordance with
local employment regulations.
